$comment: The .claude/settings.json wiring for lypning, as a standalone fragment.

`lypning install` merges exactly these three entries into an existing settings.json — appending, never rewriting, and only when no entry with the same command is already there. This file is for the other case: a user who would rather paste it in themselves, and a reviewer who wants to see what the merge intends before running it.
MERGE, DO NOT REPLACE. If the file already has a "hooks" object, add these entries to it; dropping this object over the top of it costs the user every hook they already had.

The commands are two-part on purpose: `sh "$CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR/.claude/hooks/<name>.sh"` for a project install, `sh "$HOME/.claude/hooks/<name>.sh"` for a user-scope one. A wheel that ships without the shell scripts is a supported shape — wire the CLI entry points instead (`lypning hook pre-tool-use`, `lypning hook stop`, `lypning shim install`), which do the same work one exec later and cost the shell screen that makes the PreToolUse hook affordable.

Every one of these prints {"continue":true,"suppressOutput":true} and exits 0 on every path, including its own failures. There is deliberately no permissionDecision field anywhere here: answering "allow" from a PreToolUse hook would bypass the permission prompt for every Bash command in the session, which is a far bigger change than a capture harness is allowed to make.
Off switches, no edit required: LYPNING_CAPTURE=0 disables the whole harness, LYPNING_HARVEST=0 keeps capturing but stops the Stop hook publishing.
